newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee up 2.7 pct in REER in February-RBI.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee up 2.7 pct in REER in February-RBI.

text.p: The rupee appreciated by 2.7 percent as per the real effective exchange rate (REER) index in February 1997, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Monday.
The rupee's REER in trade-based weights rose to 64.86 in February 1997 from 63.18 in January 1997, the Reserve Bank of India bulletin for June 1997 said.
"This appreciation is for the month of February alone," said an economist at a securities firm in Bombay.
"The cumulative appreciation will be much more," he said.
The rupee nominal effective exchange rate (NEER) also rose during the period, the RBI document said.
The NEER rose by 2.1 percent to 39.22 in February from 38.41 in January 1997, RBI said.
"The REER takes 1985 as the base year, which is not an ideal base," said an economist. He said 1993, when the rupee was partially floated, would be a better base for the index.
"If you rebase the REER on 1993, the rupee is up about 6.7 percent," he said.
The rupee has held firm against the dollar over the last year despite the dollar's rise against major global currencies.
